answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on per-identity stake bond plus peer re-execution of every receipt. Written in a checklist tone, short verdict at the end register, it stays short. A ember of per-task receipts records who did what, and the tundra of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The cipher of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
